newsitem.title: USA: Dominick's Supermarkets files for offering.
newsitem.headline: Dominick's Supermarkets files for offering.

text.p: Dominick's Supermarkets Inc said Friday it filed a registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission for an initial public offering of common stock.
The offering includes sales by certain Dominick's stockholders and an underwriter option to purchase additional shares to cover any over-allotments.
The number of shares to be sold was not specified.
Dominick's said it plans to apply for a listing of its stock on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol DFF.
Dominick's, the second largest supermarket operator in the Chicago market, had fiscal 1995 revenues of $2.4 billion and 97 stores operating under the Dominick's and Omni names.

Earlier, the company's Dominick's Finer Foods operating subsidiary reported sales for the third quarter ended August 3 of $759.3 million, up from $739.0 million a year ago. Sales for the first nine months of the fiscal year were $1.90 billion, up from $1.89 billion.
Sales increased due to the rise in comparable store sales and the exclusion of the week following Easter, which is historically a weak sales period.
Gross profit for the quarter totaled $176.1 million, up from $168.1 million. For the nine-months, the gross profit rose to $437.0 million from $421.8 million.
The company attributed the increase in gross profit margin primarily to the favorable impact of its purchasing improvement program and enhanced perishable and drug department margins.
The offering will be made by an underwriting group led by Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp. Morgan Stanley & Co Inc, BT Securities Corp and Chase Securities Inc will serve as co-managers.
Dominick's said net proceeds from the shares will be used primarily to retire all of its outstanding 15 percent redeemable exchangeable cumulative preferred stock.
The company said it also intends to repay outstanding bank borrowings, together with available cash and borrowings anticipated under a new credit facility.
